title: SLO guardrail composer for staged model rollouts
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Problem: We need an automated, interpretable mechanism to combine multiple operational signals (latency p95, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput) into rollback decisions for canary/A-B/staged model rollouts. Existing heuristics are brittle: fixed thresholds cause noisy rollbacks during traffic bursts, and single-signal triggers miss correlated degradations (e.g., small latency rise + cost spike).

Proposal summary: Build an SLO Guardrail Composer (SGC) that fuses signals into a configurable policy DSL and computes a composite rollback score. Key pieces: signal normalization (percentile-based baselines), time-window decay (EWMA), statistical significance checks (sequential hypothesis/Bayesian change detection), and severity scaling to weigh cost versus latency. The SGC provides both automated actions (immediate rollback, traffic cutover, staged pause) and advisory alerts for manual operator confirmation.

Core features: 1) Multi-signal fusion: p95 latency delta, 5xx error rate delta, average token cost delta, and throughput degradation. 2) Baseline model: for each signal compute expected distribution from rolling baseline window (configurable 1h/6h/24h) and use percentile deltas (e.g., p95 -> p95 delta) rather than absolute values. 3) Composite rollback score: normalized z-score-like transforms per signal, weighted sum with tunable weights per project/customer. 4) Adaptive thresholds: threshold as function of traffic volume and statistical confidence; uses a minimal effect size and p-value / Bayes factor guard to avoid acting on noise. 5) Canary ramps are coupled with dynamic tolerances: early ramp stages (0-1%) use tighter error tolerances and looser cost tolerances; mid ramp stages adjust weights. 6) Shadow traffic handling: SGC tracks divergence between shadow and production variants and uses divergence as input to rollback decision.

Intended outcomes: more robust rollbacks with fewer false positives, faster detection of genuine regressions that manifest across signals, and operator-visible reasoning traces for every automated action.

Architecture notes: SGC runs as a service in the control plane. It subscribes to metrics streams (Console metrics, tracing, token billing) and writes decisions to rollout controller (canary manager) via a small policy API. All decisions are logged to the event store and tied to rollout IDs for replay and post-mortem.

Operational safety: automated rollback actions are gated behind two independent checks: (A) statistical confidence check (default Bayes factor > 10 or p < 0.01 after sequential correction) AND (B) composite score above rollout-stage-specific threshold. For high-impact customers or Dedicated deployments the default action is advisory until customer enables auto-rollback.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SGC can ingest latency, errors, token-cost, and throughput for a rollout and compute a composite rollback score every 30s.
2) For synthetic regressions we inject a +30% p95 latency and +0.5% absolute 5xx increase; SGC triggers advisory alert within 2 minutes and automated rollback within 5 minutes when auto-rollback enabled.
3) False positive rate: during a 72h production baseline run with real traffic, automated rollback must not trigger more than once per 30 days on default config.
4) Admin UI exposes weights, baseline window, and per-stage thresholds; changes persist and apply to ongoing rollouts.
5) All automated actions produce a traceable event with contributing signal breakdown and confidence scores that are queryable in Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev prototyping): implement scoring library and unit tests; local sim harness with replayed traces (2 weeks). Phase 2 (internal canary): integrate with canary manager, run on 0.1% of internal traffic with advisory-only mode (3 weeks). Phase 3 (opt-in customers): enable auto-rollback for select customers with dedicated config and extended observability (2 weeks). Phase 4 (default enablement): broaden to platform default with tuned thresholds and runbook updates (4 weeks).
telemetry_and_signals: Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, request rate, 4xx/5xx counts, token cost per request, model-run CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates. Derived signals: delta from baseline (fractional), normalized z-scores, EWMA-smoothed trends, divergence between shadow and prod embeddings (cosine distance distribution). Logging: decision event with contributing signals and rationale, rollout id, timestamp, actor (automation or user).
tuning_strategy: Start with conservative defaults: require both a composite score > 3.0 and Bayes factor > 10 for automated rollback. Provide a calibration tool that runs historical replays to recommend weights and minimal effect sizes for a given workload. Expose a per-project 'sensitivity' knob (low/medium/high) that maps to multiplier on thresholds. Support CI-driven preflight: when uploading a new model, run a synthetic micro-benchmark suite to precompute expected signal baselines. Use sequential testing (alpha spending) to control false discovery during multi-stage ramps.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and normalization. Integration tests with canary manager in test cluster. Fault-injection: simulate clock skew, missing metrics, and transient downstream spikes to validate guards. Long-run replay: 14-day historical replay to assert false-positive rate. User acceptance: run with internal SRE team for 2 sprints and collect feedback.
open_questions: 1) How to represent cost SLO tradeoffs in customer-configurable terms (absolute token budget vs per-response cost)? 2) Should we support per-route or per-model baselines by default? 3) For Dedicated deployments with private metrics pipelines, what minimal telemetry contract is required? 4) How to chain rollback actions (soft pause -> partial rollback -> full rollback) while preserving state?
